entry.title: Time to watch before joining
entry.summary: Let your child stay near you and look around when a social setting feels unfamiliar. Davies offers support without trying to change a quieter temperament.
entry.cue: They may watch from beside you instead of going straight into the group.
detail: Beforehand, describe a little of what will happen. On arrival, show them around or allow time at your side while you carry on an ordinary conversation.

Davies suggests small supported practice when it is useful, such as trying a greeting or words for “stop.” The purpose is helping the child handle a situation, not comparing them with a more outgoing child.
An early arrival or shorter visit is another possibility when a busy group is difficult.
